assessment.evidence: Coverage revision 003 maps all 21 human-confirmed obligation clusters for GDPR, conditional SFDR, conditional AIFMD and the EU AI Act and all four conditional DORA clusters to active requirements. Official-source, date and article-level mappings remain explicitly owned validation work.

SR-009 and VAL-001 preserve entity-specific applicability or exemption as General Counsel work, require interim ICT risk, incident, resilience and provider-oversight evidence, and prohibit formal DORA compliance claims.

DR-007 now translates highly-confidential handling; SR-001, SR-002 and SR-007 govern location, transfer and privileged access; SR-010 translates EU/member-state legal governance and foreign-exposure assessment and acceptance. VAL-005 retains the approved-location and exception-evidence detail with General Counsel.

DR-002 through DR-007 and SR-002/SR-003 cover licensing, minimisation, special-category exclusion, provenance, retention, legal holds, working-copy deletion, transfer governance, training prohibition and classification-bound handling. Exact source schedules and privacy evidence remain owned validation work.

FR-002, AR-001, AR-002, SR-006, NR-001 and NR-002 define assistive use, required review, retained decision authority, prohibited actions, citations, unsupported-claim thresholds, risk detection, logging and auditable review. No unsupported AI risk classification is asserted.

All 31 active requirements are sourced and have stable acceptance tests. T-DR-007 and T-SR-010 directly test the remediated outcomes. SR-008 assigns the independent verdict to Internal Audit. VAL-002 through VAL-005 retain definitions and operational evidence needed before execution.

DORA, AI classification, service definitions, benchmark definitions, source mappings and approved-location details have named accountable owners, validation timing and change-control consequences; none is presented as waived or complete.
The candidate claims no architecture, Azure service, deployment, runtime result, AI risk classification, formal DORA compliance, certification, attestation or Phase 1 approval.

verdictRationale: The prior major traceability defect is resolved by active, sourced and testable DR-007 and SR-010. Complete current coverage maps all 21 confirmed and four conditional obligation clusters; DORA remains correctly conditional; privacy, sovereignty, AI safety, independent acceptance and unsupported-claim boundaries are explicit. No blocker or major finding remains. The retained legal-source, DORA, AI-classification and operational validation gaps are visible, owner-bound and not waived, so a gap-qualified rather than unqualified conforming verdict is appropriate.
